exec: Political pressure is building over the outages; officials uniformly say no cyberattack is involved.
plain: US politicians want answers about the run of outages. The President, the spy chief, the homeland security chief and the White House all say it was not a cyberattack.

sources.name: BNN Bloomberg / CTV News live updates

summary: Lawmakers are pressing for explanations after outages at Microsoft, the FAA, major banks, Apple and the NSA. Senate Democrats want the FAA's router replacement paused, and Majority Leader John Thune said the US must step up efforts against outages. President Trump, in Manila, said "It's fine." DNI Jay Clayton, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and the White House all said they see no cyberattack; Clayton tied the outages to system upgrades.
title: Washington reacts to the outages: lawmakers demand answers, DHS chief points to AI

validation.note: Two outlets report the political response.
